definitions.explanation: A body or form that is soft and flexible, lacking hard skeletal structure. Most commonly encountered in the compound {軟体動物|なんたいどうぶつ} (mollusk), but also used independently to describe flexibility.

examples.japanese: タコは{軟体|なんたい}{動物|どうぶつ}です。
{軟体|なんたい}{動物|どうぶつ}は{骨|ほね}がないため{狭|せま}い{隙間|すきま}にも{入|はい}れる。
examples.english: Soft-bodied animals have no bones, so they can fit into narrow gaps.

examples.japanese: イカや{貝|かい}など、{軟体|なんたい}{動物|どうぶつ}の{種類|しゅるい}は{世界中|せかいじゅう}に{約|やく}10{万|まん}{種|しゅ}いると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that there are approximately 100,000 species of mollusks, including squid and shellfish, worldwide.

notes:
Combines {軟|なん} (soft) and {体|たい} (body). Almost always encountered in the compound {軟体動物|なんたいどうぶつ} (mollusks — the phylum Mollusca), which includes snails, clams, octopuses, and squid. Also used figuratively to describe a person with unusual flexibility.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {軟体|なんたい}{動物|どうぶつ}: mollusk (the most common usage)
- {軟体|なんたい}{動物|どうぶつ}{門|もん}: phylum Mollusca
- {軟体|なんたい}{生物|せいぶつ}: soft-bodied organism

RELATED WORDS:
- {節足|せっそく}{動物|どうぶつ}: arthropod — another major invertebrate group
- {甲殻|こうかく}{類|るい}: crustaceans — hard-shelled invertebrates, in contrast to soft-bodied ones
